edges.description: Aberrant salience attributed to internal representations is experienced directly as hallucination. The intermediate step is psychological rather than neurochemical, which is why this is not a direct link.
Delusions arise as the patient's explanatory response to aberrantly salient experience, so the dopaminergic state reaches this phenotype through an interposed cognitive step.

NMDA receptors on fast-spiking parvalbumin interneurons are the first casualty of receptor hypofunction; losing their excitatory drive disinhibits the pyramidal cells they normally restrain. This is the step that makes the glutamatergic and GABAergic nodes one circuit rather than two parallel abnormalities.

NMDA antagonists reproduce formal thought disorder in humans, which dopaminergic psychotomimetics do not — the observation that first separated the glutamatergic model from the dopamine model on symptom coverage.
NMDA receptor blockade produces the negative-symptom domain, including emotional withdrawal, in people with no psychiatric illness.
Blunted affect is part of the negative-symptom picture NMDA antagonism reproduces in healthy volunteers.

Loss of interneuron restraint leaves pyramidal cells overactive, and that overactivity — hippocampal in particular — drives the subcortical hyperdopaminergic state. This is the edge that makes the cortical and dopaminergic halves of the entry one graph: it is how a cortical lesion produces a striatal symptom.

Parvalbumin basket-cell inhibition of pyramidal cells is what generates prefrontal gamma oscillations, and those oscillations are required for working memory. The deficit is a direct functional consequence of the inhibitory abnormality, not a downstream dopaminergic effect — which is why antipsychotics do not treat it.

Prefrontal M1 signalling supports working memory and verbal learning, and a muscarinic agonist improved exactly those measures in patients — an inference from therapeutic response rather than a direct demonstration that the receptor deficit causes the impairment.
Reduced M4-mediated cholinergic braking releases striatal dopamine release from restraint, feeding the dopaminergic dysregulation that drives positive symptoms.

edges.description: Excessive complement- and microglia-mediated synapse elimination can disrupt cortical pyramidal-neuron circuits and disinhibit mesostriatal projections, providing an indirect route from adolescent synaptic loss to dopamine overactivity and psychosis.

The synapses removed are overwhelmingly cortical excitatory ones, so over-pruning is a route into the glutamatergic node as well as the dopaminergic one. The same sentence of the synaptic-hypothesis review carries both arms: pyramidal-neuron dysfunction here, mesostriatal disinhibition on the dopamine edge above.

Parvalbumin interneurons are the cortical cell type most exposed to redox stress — their high firing rate and metabolic load make them the first to fail when glutathione synthesis is impaired. This is the node's route into the cortical circuit, and it is why an antioxidant is a candidate treatment for a GABAergic lesion.

evidence.reference_title: GABA-ergic neurons and the neurobiology of schizophrenia and other psychoses.
evidence.snippet: At the cellular level, gamma-aminobutyric acid (GABA)-ergic interneurons are a common feature in psychotic states... and are themselves synchronised by the ascending dopamine and serotonin innervations.

evidence.snippet: Gamma-aminobutyric acid (GABA) is the main inhibitory neurotransmitter in the brain. GABAergic receptor abnormalities have been documented in several major psychiatric disorders including schizophrenia.

evidence.reference_title: Synaptic dysfunction in schizophrenia.
evidence.snippet: Here, we will review evidence for altered neurotransmission at ... GABAergic ... synapses in schizophrenia...

nodes.description: Dysfunction in glutamate neurotransmission, impacting synaptic plasticity and brain circuit function.

evidence.reference_title: The emerging role of glutamate in the pathophysiology and treatment of schizophrenia.
evidence.snippet: Research has implicated dysfunction of glutamatergic neurotransmission in the pathophysiology of schizophrenia.

evidence.reference_title: Mapping the Consequences of Impaired Synaptic Plasticity in Schizophrenia through Development: An Integrative Model for Diverse Clinical Features.
evidence.snippet: Accumulating evidence suggests that synaptic plasticity is impaired in schizophrenia. Given the role of synaptic plasticity in learning, memory, and neural circuit maturation, impaired plasticity may underlie many features of the schizophrenia syndrome.

evidence.reference_title: Beyond the dopamine hypothesis of schizophrenia to three neural networks of psychosis: dopamine, serotonin, and glutamate.
evidence.snippet: Psychosis is now widely hypothesized to involve neural networks beyond the classical dopaminergic mesolimbic pathway, including serotonin and glutamate systems as well.

evidence.reference_title: Synaptic dysfunction in schizophrenia.
evidence.snippet: Schizophrenia is believed to result from problems during neural development that lead to improper function of synaptic transmission and plasticity, and in agreement, many of the susceptibility genes encode proteins critical for neural development.

nodes.description: Medications such as risperidone, olanzapine, and clozapine to manage symptoms.

evidence.reference_title: Current status of antipsychotic treatment.
evidence.snippet: With the use of chlorpromazine and other traditional antipsychotics for psychosis, it was soon discovered that the antipsychotic efficacy of this class of medications was closely associated with their ability to block dopamine D(2) receptors in the brain.

evidence.reference_title: Management of schizophrenia.
evidence.snippet: The introduction of novel antipsychotic agents, such as clozapine and risperidone, has enhanced the clinicians' ability to manage schizophrenic patients.

evidence.reference_title: Treatment-resistant schizophrenic patients.
evidence.snippet: Clozapine has shown to be effective in some poor or partially responsive patients in three prospective, random assignment, double-blind trials.

evidence.reference_title: Blood plasma proteomic modulation induced by olanzapine and risperidone in schizophrenia patients.
evidence.snippet: To improve treatment efficacy during the critical early stages of schizophrenia, we aimed to identify molecular signatures at baseline (T0) for prediction of a positive response to the atypical antipsychotics olanzapine and risperidone after 6 weeks (T6) treatment.

evidence.reference_title: Schizophrenia endophenotypes as treatment targets.
evidence.snippet: The drug discovery process has focused mostly on targeting D2 dopamine receptors.

evidence.reference_title: Clinical practice guidelines for management of schizophrenia in India: A comprehensive overview.
evidence.snippet: Pharmacological strategies emphasize rational antipsychotic use, including early intervention principles, maintenance treatment, long-acting injectable antipsychotics, therapeutic drug monitoring-particularly for clozapine

evidence.reference_title: Schizophrenia, the prefrontal cortex, and a mechanism of genetic susceptibility.
evidence.snippet: COMT is an enzyme that is distributed widely throughout the brain, but seems to be uniquely relevant to how dopamine affects information-processing in the prefrontal cortex. There is a common variation in the genetic sequence of the COMT gene, which causes a dramatic change in its enzyme activity. In people with schizophrenia, in their healthy siblings, and also in normal controls, the COMT genotype predicts 4% of the variation in human executive cognition and working memory. We have thus identified a genetic mechanism in the human species that affects the efficiency and efficacy of information-processing in the prefrontal cortex. It is, also, a weak genetic risk factor for schizophrenia: in family studies, it increases the risk of schizophrenia by 50-80%.

nodes.description: Excessive elimination of synapses by microglia via complement component C4A and CR3 pathways during adolescent brain development.

evidence.reference_title: Schizophrenia risk from complex variation of complement component 4.
evidence.snippet: We found that these alleles generated widely varying levels of C4A and C4B expression in the brain, with each common C4 allele associating with schizophrenia in proportion to its tendency to generate greater expression of C4A.

evidence.reference_title: The synaptic hypothesis of schizophrenia version III: a master mechanism.
evidence.snippet: Genome-wide association studies have identified a number of schizophrenia risk variants converging on pathways regulating synaptic elimination, formation and plasticity, including complement factors and microglial-mediated synaptic pruning.

evidence.reference_title: Increased synapse elimination by microglia in schizophrenia patient-derived models of synaptic pruning.
evidence.snippet: Using a reprogrammed in vitro model of microglia-mediated synapse engulfment, we demonstrate increased synapse elimination in patient-derived neural cultures and isolated synaptosomes.

evidence.reference_title: Overexpression of schizophrenia susceptibility factor human complement C4A promotes excessive synaptic loss and behavioral changes in mice.
evidence.snippet: However, overexpressing C4A in mice reduced cortical synapse density, increased microglial engulfment of synapses and altered mouse behavior.

evidence.reference_title: Microglia-neuron interactions in schizophrenia.
evidence.snippet: Synaptic loss, one of the central pathological hallmarks of schizophrenia, is believed to be due to excess removal of synapses by activated microglia, primarily affecting glutamatergic neurons.

nodes.description: Selective loss of M1 muscarinic acetylcholine receptor protein, mRNA and pirenzepine binding in dorsolateral prefrontal cortex (Brodmann area 9). The deficit is bimodally rather than uniformly distributed: kernel density estimation separates a distinct postmortem subgroup — muscarinic receptor-deficit schizophrenia (MRDS) — at roughly a quarter of cases, with a ~74% reduction in cortical binding, from a non-MRDS majority whose binding overlaps controls.

biological_processes: muscarinic acetylcholine receptor signalling in prefrontal cortex

evidence.reference_title: Decreased muscarinic1 receptors in the dorsolateral prefrontal cortex of subjects with schizophrenia.
evidence.snippet: The level of M1R protein (0.11 +/- 0.007 vs 0.15 +/- 0.008 OD; P < 0.01), but not M4R protein, was decreased in BA9 from schizophrenic subjects with neither receptor protein being altered in BA 40.

evidence.reference_title: Decreased cortical muscarinic receptors define a subgroup of subjects with schizophrenia.
evidence.snippet: We suggest that these individuals make up 'muscarinic receptor-deficit schizophrenia' (MRDS).

evidence.reference_title: In vivo determination of muscarinic acetylcholine receptor availability in schizophrenia.
evidence.snippet: Muscarinic receptor availability was significantly less in patients with schizophrenia than in normal subjects in all regions of interest except the pons.

nodes.description: Neurons carrying SETD1A loss-of-function alleles accumulate DNA double-strand breaks, preferentially at long neural genes. SETD1A occupies DNA damage-prone sites in both neural progenitors and postmitotic neurons, so the instability tracks where the methyltransferase normally acts rather than being a nonspecific consequence of illness.

evidence.reference_title: SETD1A regulates psychiatric gene networks involved in genomic stability and synaptic function in rare and sporadic schizophrenia.
evidence.snippet: Additionally, SETD1A binds to DNA damage-prone sites in neural progenitor cells and postmitotic neurons.

evidence.reference_title: Delusions beyond beliefs: a critical overview of diagnostic, aetiological, and therapeutic schizophrenia research from a clinical-phenomenological perspective.
evidence.snippet: Delusions are commonly conceived as false beliefs that are held with certainty and which cannot be corrected. This conception of delusion has been influential throughout the history of psychiatry and continues to inform how delusions are approached in clinical practice and in contemporary schizophrenia research.

evidence.reference_title: The Capgras phenomenon.
evidence.snippet: The underlying diagnosis of Capgras delusion is not found to be exclusively paranoid schizophrenia, nor is the sex exclusively female, as once was believed.

evidence.reference_title: De Clérambault Syndrome, Othello Syndrome, Folie à Deux and Variants.
evidence.snippet: Non-bizarre delusion, defined as a false belief possible although highly unlikely, is the main manifestation of delusional disorders, previously known as paranoia.

evidence.reference_title: Unravelling offending in schizophrenia: factors characterising subgroups of offenders.
evidence.snippet: Persecutory and/or grandiose delusions were more strongly associated with each offender group compared with non-offenders, most so with late first offenders.

evidence.reference_title: [Impairments of language and communication in schizophrenia].
evidence.snippet: Disorganized speech is one of the key symptoms of schizophrenia. This article provides an overview of those areas of speech and communication impaired in patients with schizophrenia.

evidence.reference_title: Studies of the course of schizophasia.
evidence.snippet: The course of psychoses of schizophrenic type follows rules which are still not adequately understood. It is, however, clear that certain symptoms appear mostly early, others only late... we studied 44 final phase patients whose main symptom was disordered thinking of the schizophasic type.

evidence.reference_title: Deficits in Analytic and Common-Sense Reasoning in Schizophrenia.
evidence.snippet: Patients with schizophrenia were impaired in both analytic and common-sense thinking.

evidence.reference_title: Syntactic complexity of spoken language in the diagnosis of schizophrenia: A probabilistic Bayes network model.
evidence.snippet: We conclude that an early drift towards linguistic disorganization/impoverishment of clause complexity-at the granular level of nominal subject per clause-is a distinctive feature of schizophrenia that decreases longitudinally, thus differentiating schizophrenia from other psychotic illnesses with shared phenomenology.

evidence.reference_title: Delusional thinking and cognitive disorder.
evidence.snippet: The data of interest are (a) the failure to find evidence of cognitive impairment in diagnosed paranoid patients...

nodes.description: Imbalance in dopamine transmission in the brain, particularly in the mesolimbic and mesocortical pathways.

evidence.reference_title: Pathway-Specific Dopamine Abnormalities in Schizophrenia.
evidence.snippet: Findings have converged to suggest early dysregulation in the striatum, especially in the rostral caudate, manifesting as excess synthesis and release. Recent data showed deficit extending to most cortical regions and even to other extrastriatal subcortical regions not previously considered to be 'hypodopaminergic' in schizophrenia.

evidence.reference_title: A neurobiological hypothesis for the classification of schizophrenia: type A (hyperdopaminergic) and type B (normodopaminergic).
evidence.snippet: A neurobiological hypothesis for the classification of schizophrenia: type A (hyperdopaminergic) and type B (normodopaminergic).

evidence.reference_title: Schizophrenia: a subcortical neurotransmitter imbalance syndrome?
evidence.snippet: This article discusses the possibility that a deficient activity within the cortico-striatal glutamatergic pathway is an important pathophysiological component in some cases of schizophrenia and that glutamatergic agonists may prove beneficial in this disorder.

evidence.reference_title: Is schizophrenia a dopamine supersensitivity psychotic reaction?
evidence.snippet: This clinical picture is generally associated with supersensitivity to dopamine, and activates dopamine neurotransmission that is usually alleviated or blocked by drugs that block dopamine D2 receptors.

evidence.reference_title: Flat affect in schizophrenia: relation to emotion processing and neurocognitive measures.
evidence.snippet: Impaired emotional functioning in schizophrenia is a prominent clinical feature that manifests primarily as flat affect... Flat affect was more common in men and was associated with poorer premorbid adjustment, worse current quality of life, and worse outcome at 1-year follow-up.

evidence.reference_title: Clinical phenotypes of psychosis in the Bipolar-Schizophrenia Network on Intermediate Phenotypes (B-SNIP).
evidence.snippet: Schizophrenia probands showed more symptoms and lower psychosocial functioning than probands with psychotic bipolar disorder, but there was considerable overlap in clinical manifestations.

evidence.reference_title: Voice patterns in schizophrenia: A systematic review and Bayesian meta-analysis.
evidence.snippet: Voice atypicalities have been a characteristic feature of schizophrenia ... They are often associated with core negative symptoms such as flat affect and alogia ... This suggests that voice atypicalities may represent a marker of clinical features and social functioning in schizophrenia.

evidence.reference_title: Animal models for the negative symptoms of schizophrenia.
evidence.snippet: In schizophrenia, negative symptoms encompass, among others, anhedonia, flat affect, avolition, and social withdrawal.

evidence.reference_title: Emotional word usage in groups at risk for schizophrenia-spectrum disorders: An objective investigation of attention to emotion.
evidence.snippet: Both extreme levels of social anhedonia (SocAnh) and extreme levels of perceptual aberration/magical ideation (PerMag) indicate increased risk for schizophrenia-spectrum disorders and are associated with emotional deficits.

evidence.reference_title: Defining the schizophrenia phenotype.
evidence.snippet: The schizophrenia phenotype has been traditionally defined by chronic psychosis and functional deterioration ... Subtle clinical signs and symptoms, cognitive impairment particularly in attention and memory, and neurophysiologic deficits such as in sensory gating and smooth-pursuit eye movements all define aspects of the schizophrenia phenotype.

evidence.reference_title: Psychotic and Bipolar Disorders: Schizophrenia.
evidence.snippet: Schizophrenia symptoms fall into six common symptom clusters: delusions and hallucinations, disorganization of speech, cognitive dysfunction, negative symptoms, affective symptoms, and motor system abnormalities.

evidence.reference_title: Ophthalmology issues in schizophrenia.
evidence.snippet: Schizophrenia is a complex mental disorder associated with not only cognitive dysfunctions, such as memory and attention deficits, but also changes in basic sensory processing.

evidence.reference_title: Clinical correlates of olfactory hallucinations in schizophrenia.
evidence.snippet: Prevalence of OHs and hallucinations in other modalities differed according to the WHO-10 international centre. Across centres, OHs were present in 13% of the WHO-10 dataset, similar to the 17% prevalence rate in the SAPS/SANS dataset.

evidence.reference_title: Auditory Verbal Hallucinations in Schizophrenia, Part II: Phenomenological Qualities and Evolution.
evidence.snippet: We found that a substantial proportion of patients could not clearly distinguish between thinking and hallucinating. The emotional tone of the voices increased in negativity.

nodes.description: Cholinergic input to the striatum and substantia nigra normally holds dopaminergic transmission in check through the M4 muscarinic receptor: M4 activation on spiny projection neurons produces a sustained depression of striatal dopamine release, and nigral M4 opposes D1 signalling in direct-pathway presynaptic terminals. Weakened M4 restraint is proposed to permit the striatal dopamine dysregulation that generates positive symptoms, and supplies the mechanistic route by which a non-D2 muscarinic agonist reaches the canonical dopamine node.

biological_processes: muscarinic restraint of striatal dopamine release

evidence.reference_title: Cholinergic Projections to the Substantia Nigra Pars Reticulata Inhibit Dopamine Modulation of Basal Ganglia through the M(4) Muscarinic Receptor.
evidence.snippet: extra-striatal cholinergic projections from the pedunculopontine nucleus to the substantia nigra pars reticulata (SNr) act on muscarinic acetylcholine receptor subtype 4 (M4) to oppose cAMP-dependent dopamine receptor subtype 1 (D1) signaling in presynaptic terminals of direct pathway striatal spiny projections neurons

evidence.reference_title: In vivo determination of muscarinic acetylcholine receptor availability in schizophrenia.
evidence.snippet: Positive symptoms of schizophrenia correlated negatively with muscarinic receptor availability in the striatum and the frontal cortex.

nodes.description: Bioenergetic deficits including complex I inhibition, decreased glutathione, increased lactate, and oxidative/nitrosative stress creating a feed-forward cycle with neuroinflammation.

evidence.reference_title: Mitochondrial dysfunction in schizophrenia: With a focus on postmortem studies.
evidence.snippet: Decreased activity of complexes I and IV are prominent as well as abnormal levels of individual subunits that comprise the complexes of the electron transport chain.

nodes.description: SETD1A deposits H3K4 methylation at active promoters, and it binds those promoters selectively at schizophrenia risk loci controlling chromatin remodeling, DNA repair, and synaptic function. Loss-of-function variants reduce that activity directly. The same deficit is reached without a rare variant in sporadic disease, where cortical SETD1A expression is low and SETD1A-regulated genes are correspondingly downregulated, which is why this node is curated as a mechanism of schizophrenia rather than as an annotation on the mutation carriers.
nodes.id: Reduced SETD1A H3K4 Methyltransferase Activity at Psychiatric Risk Gene Promoters

evidence.reference_title: SETD1A regulates psychiatric gene networks involved in genomic stability and synaptic function in rare and sporadic schizophrenia.
evidence.snippet: SETD1A preferentially binds the promoters of polygenic risk loci for psychiatric disorders that regulate chromatin remodeling, DNA repair, and synaptic function

evidence.reference_title: SETD1A regulates psychiatric gene networks involved in genomic stability and synaptic function in rare and sporadic schizophrenia.
evidence.snippet: In postmortem SCZ cortical tissue, individuals who lack SETD1A mutations exhibit reduced SETD1A expression, associated with downregulation of SETD1A-regulated genes, implicating SETD1A-H3K4me dysfunction in sporadic SCZ cases.

evidence.reference_title: Social Life in the Schizophrenia Spectrum: A Phenomenological Study of Five Patients.
evidence.snippet: A 'positively withdrawn' position characterizes a wider group of patients than originally reported. Further, we identified a preference for partaking in social activities in particular circumstances with clearly circumscribed goals or social roles and rules.

evidence.reference_title: Social withdrawal and neurocognitive correlates in schizophrenia.
evidence.snippet: Social withdrawal was measured by a specific item of the Heinrichs-Carpenter Quality of Life Scale. Social withdrawal was associated with a lower score in the neurocognitive composite score and in 'Verbal memory,' 'Processing speed' and 'Working memory' scores.

evidence.reference_title: Animal models for the negative symptoms of schizophrenia.
evidence.snippet: Negative symptoms encompass, among others, anhedonia, flat affect, avolition and social withdrawal.

evidence.reference_title: Social Disconnection in Schizophrenia and the General Community.
evidence.snippet: Social disability is a defining characteristic of schizophrenia... One component, social disconnection, occurs extensively... Social disconnection is an objective, long-standing lack of social/family relationships and minimal participation in social activities.

evidence.reference_title: Evidence that a working memory cognitive phenotype within schizophrenia has a unique underlying biology.
evidence.snippet: Our data gives preliminary support to the hypotheses that there is a working memory deficit phenotype within the syndrome of schizophrenia with has a biological underpinning.

evidence.reference_title: Posterior Parietal Cortex Dysfunction Is Central to Working Memory Storage and Broad Cognitive Deficits in Schizophrenia.
evidence.snippet: PFC dysfunction is widely believed to underlie working memory (WM) deficits in people with schizophrenia (PSZ)...These results indicate that PPC dysfunction is central to WM storage deficits in PSZ and may play a key role in the broad cognitive deficits associated with schizophrenia.

evidence.reference_title: Iconic decay in schizophrenia.
evidence.snippet: Working memory impairment is considered a core deficit in schizophrenia.

evidence.reference_title: Schizophrenia, "just the facts" 4. Clinical features and conceptualization.
evidence.snippet: It is characterized by an admixture of positive, negative, cognitive, mood, and motor symptoms whose severity varies across patients and through the course of the illness.

nodes.description: First-in-class M1/M4 muscarinic receptor agonist (xanomeline) combined with the peripherally-restricted pan-muscarinic antagonist trospium chloride to mitigate peripheral cholinergic side effects. FDA-approved September 2024 for schizophrenia in adults, marketed as Cobenfy. Acts without direct D2 dopamine-receptor blockade, demonstrating that effective antipsychotic activity can be achieved through a non-dopaminergic mechanism.

evidence.reference_title: Long-term efficacy, safety, and tolerability of xanomeline and trospium chloride in schizophrenia: A 52-week, open-label trial (EMERGENT-5).
evidence.snippet: The M1/M4 muscarinic receptor agonist xanomeline combined with the peripherally restricted pan-muscarinic receptor antagonist trospium chloride is the first approved treatment for adults with schizophrenia with no direct D2 dopamine receptor blockade.

evidence.reference_title: Efficacy and safety of the muscarinic receptor agonist KarXT (xanomeline-trospium) in schizophrenia (EMERGENT-2) in the USA: results from a randomised, double-blind, placebo-controlled, flexible-dose phase 3 trial.
evidence.snippet: The trial met the primary endpoint with a mean change from baseline to week 5 in PANSS total score that favoured KarXT (-21·2 points, SE 1·7) versus placebo (-11·6 points, 1·6; least squares mean difference -9·6; 95% CI -13·9 to -5·2; p<0·0001, Cohen's d effect size=0·61).

evidence.reference_title: Efficacy and Safety of Xanomeline-Trospium Chloride in Schizophrenia: A Randomized Clinical Trial.
evidence.snippet: These findings, together with the previously reported and consistent results from the EMERGENT-1 and EMERGENT-2 trials, support the potential of xanomeline-trospium to be the first in a putative new class of antipsychotic medications without D2 dopamine receptor blocking activity.
